chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, all from al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The people in the early times, whenever they found something and took it, it would be withheld (from them); they would not be able to take a step until they threw it back, so its seeker would come after them and take it. And indeed, the people have become audacious in what is more than that, and it beyond that, and it will return to being as it was.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on found property according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes a divine mechanism in early Islamic times where a finder of lost property was physically restrained until the owner claimed it, serving as a tangible deterrent against greed. He notes that as people became more audacious in appropriating found items, this miraculous withholding ceased, yet he prophesies its return, a belief often linked to the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him) and the establishment of true justice. This narration highlights the transition from supernatural enforcement of property rights to legalistic frameworks, emphasizing the spiritual integrity of ownership in Shia tradition.
